perType.role: The owned OS-environment read seam and the contract interface the human signs off. Gains the single decided member string GetBaseDirectory() (Decision 2), whose doc records the faithful trailing-directory-separator guarantee (Decision 5).
perType.bodies: interface-none — the new GetBaseDirectory() member has no body.

perType.role: The single REAL IEnvironment owner and the one class where raw AppContext.BaseDirectory will be legal (AG0011 already assigns that primitive to this owner). Placed in Boundaries because AppContext.BaseDirectory is OS-agnostic (Decision 2).
perType.bodies: throw — new GetBaseDirectory() throws NotSupportedException; every existing body left exactly as-is.

perType.role: The in-memory IEnvironment fake. It must implement the new interface member or the whole test build breaks, so it is part of the compiling surface; its Create factory also gains the decided baseDirectory seed parameter (Decision 3 / AG0035 Rule 2).
perType.bodies: throw — new GetBaseDirectory() throws NotSupportedException; Create signature gains string? baseDirectory = null present in the signature only (unwired — defaulting-to-home/storing/returning is IMPLEMENT behavior); all existing bodies (private ctor, fields, other getters) left exactly as-is.

findings.summary: FakeEnvironment.Create's new `baseDirectory` parameter is a dead parameter — it is never stored in a field or threaded into the private constructor, so `GetBaseDirectory()` can never be wired to return a seeded value. The contract's decided structure ('add a stored field and a Create(...) parameter... following the existing pattern for the current and temp directories') is only half-built: the parameter exists, the field and constructor plumbing do not.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs:19-25 (field list has _home/_current/_temp/_processPath/_variables/_processArchitecture/_osArchitecture — no _baseDirectory); :27-34 (private constructor's 7 parameters mirror those 7 fields exactly — no baseDirectory parameter); :73 (`Create` declares `string? baseDirectory = null`); :78-85 (the constructor call threads `currentDirectory ?? home` and `tempDirectory ?? home` through, but `baseDirectory` is never passed as an argument — it is silently dropped); :106 (`GetBaseDirectory()` throws unconditionally, with no field it could ever return). grep confirms `baseDirectory`/`BaseDirectory` appears in this file only at the XML doc (:54-55), the parameter declaration (:73), and the stub comment (:105) — never assigned or read anywhere. `dotnet build tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/AgentGuard.TestHelpers.csproj` is 0 Warning(s)/0 Error(s), so no analyzer catches this dead parameter — it survives the build gate silently and is only visible on a design/shape review.
findings.fix: Add `private readonly string _baseDirectory;` to the field list; add `string baseDirectory` to the private constructor's parameter list and assign `_baseDirectory = baseDirectory;` in the body; in `Create`, pass `baseDirectory ?? home` as that constructor argument in the same slot/pattern as `currentDirectory ?? home` and `tempDirectory ?? home`. `GetBaseDirectory()` may keep its `NotSupportedException` ARCHITECTURE-stub throw (IMPLEMENT later wires it to return `_baseDirectory`) — only the field declaration and constructor plumbing are structural surface and must land now, matching every sibling member's already-wired pattern.

refutationAttempts: Checked both new throw-bodied members (EnvironmentAdapter.GetBaseDirectory and FakeEnvironment.GetBaseDirectory) against the brief's rule that a NotSupportedException/NotImplementedException stub body is never itself a finding — confirmed both throws are correctly out of scope; the reported finding is about the missing field/constructor plumbing around the fake's stub, not the stub body.

Grepped OwnedPrimitives.cs to independently confirm AG0011 already assigns AppContext.BaseDirectory to IEnvironment/Boundaries as the contract asserts, rather than taking the contract's claim on faith — confirmed pre-existing at OwnedPrimitives.cs:253-260, so single-owner enforcement for the real primitive already holds.

Grepped FakeEnvironment.cs for every occurrence of baseDirectory/BaseDirectory to verify the parameter is genuinely unused rather than wired under a different field name — found only 3 occurrences (doc comment, parameter declaration, stub comment), none of them storage or read.

Built AgentGuard.TestHelpers in isolation to check whether an existing analyzer already catches the dead parameter, which would make it a build-gate/DRY finding rather than a SOLID design finding — build is 0 warnings/0 errors, so it is silent without this review.

Checked IEnvironment's size/cohesion for a God-interface violation given an 8th member was added to an already multi-purpose interface — ruled not a violation because Decision 2 explicitly signs off adding it to this existing owner interface; not this author's call to relitigate.
Checked for a second-path/duplicate-owner violation (rail 4) by confirming no other class reads AppContext.BaseDirectory outside EnvironmentAdapter — none found; single owner holds.

Checked EnvironmentAdapter.cs for an analogous plumbing gap — none exists there, since GetBaseDirectory() takes no constructor-time seed and will read AppContext.BaseDirectory directly at IMPLEMENT time.

findings.summary: FakeEnvironment.Create accepts a baseDirectory parameter but never forwards or stores it — the contract-named existing pattern (store the seed in a field, default via `?? home`) already used for currentDirectory/tempDirectory was not reused for baseDirectory, so the seed is silently discarded no matter what a caller passes.
findings.evidence: tests/AgentGuard.TestHelpers/FakeEnvironment.cs:19-25 (private fields: _home, _current, _temp, _processPath, _variables, _processArchitecture, _osArchitecture — no _baseDirectory) and :27-43 (private constructor parameter list: home, current, temp, processPath, variables, processArchitecture, osArchitecture — no baseDirectory param, no assignment). The public factory at :69-77 declares `string? baseDirectory = null` (documented at :54-55 exactly like the currentDirectory/tempDirectory params), but the `new FakeEnvironment(...)` call at :78-85 passes only `home, currentDirectory ?? home, tempDirectory ?? home, processPath, variables, processArchitecture, osArchitecture` — baseDirectory never appears in the call. Compare to currentDirectory/tempDirectory, each of which IS forwarded with the `?? home` default at :80-81. Contract `.dev/inprocess/2026-08-23-os-presence-check/contract-linux-policy-path.md` 'What to do' step 3 (line 49) explicitly says to add 'a stored field and a Create(...) parameter for the base directory that defaults to the home directory when not supplied, following the existing pattern for the current and temp directories' — the parameter was added but the stored field and the forwarding were not, so the named pattern was not actually reused. Verified via direct read, grep across src/tests/analyzers for any other BaseDirectory owner (none found), and codegraph_explore over GetBaseDirectory/IEnvironment/EnvironmentAdapter/FakeEnvironment confirming these are the only three implementers and no hidden duplicate exists.
findings.fix: Add a `_baseDirectory` field and a `baseDirectory` parameter to the private constructor (mirroring `_current`/`current`), assign `_baseDirectory = baseDirectory;` in the constructor body, and change the `Create()` call at :78-85 to pass `baseDirectory ?? home` — the same defaulting pattern already used for currentDirectory and tempDirectory. Whether `GetBaseDirectory()` keeps throwing `NotSupportedException` (a legal ARCHITECTURE-stage stub) or returns `_baseDirectory` directly (as every other Fake getter already does with its stored field) is IMPLEMENT's/the architect's call, but the field and constructor wiring must exist now so the seed is not silently dropped.

refutationAttempts: Searched for an existing IEnvironment-adjacent member or interface that already exposes AppContext.BaseDirectory under a different name (grep for BaseDirectory/ExecutableDirectory/AppRoot/InstallDirectory/BinDirectory/ApplicationDirectory across src/ and tests/, plus codegraph_explore over GetBaseDirectory/IEnvironment/EnvironmentAdapter/FakeEnvironment) — none found; MachinePaths.BinDirectory and ContextStorePaths.BaseDirectory(projectRoot) are confirmed unrelated same-named concepts (setup install path, snapshot-store path), not duplicates of AppContext.BaseDirectory.

Checked whether a second raw AppContext.BaseDirectory/AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory read exists outside EnvironmentAdapter that this change should have collapsed into the new owner — found one pre-existing read in analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/RepositoryFiles.cs:27, but the contract's own reuse ledger explicitly rules it untouched ('mechanism A ... never resolves the repo root'), it predates this change, and it is outside AG0011's production/test-owner scope, so it is not a new duplication introduced by this skeleton.

Traced FakeEnvironment.Create's new baseDirectory parameter end-to-end from signature (:73) through the constructor call (:78-85) to confirm whether it actually reuses the sibling currentDirectory/tempDirectory storage pattern the contract names — confirmed it does not (finding above).

Checked SystemServicesBuilder.Build()'s default Fake() wiring (:245-252) for whether it double-seeds or duplicates a base-directory default — it does not; it omits the baseDirectory argument entirely, relying on the (currently broken) default-to-home path in FakeEnvironment.Create.

Verified the AG0035 (NoLiteralFakeRootAnalyzer) rule-phase addition for the 'baseDirectory' seed parameter name matches the FakeEnvironment.Create signature exactly, so no naming mismatch/duplication was introduced between the rule and the skeleton.

Confirmed both GetBaseDirectory() stub bodies (EnvironmentAdapter.cs:49 and FakeEnvironment.cs:106) are identical throw-NotSupportedException placeholders — treated this as the sanctioned unimplemented-body pattern, not a duplication finding, per the task's explicit carve-out.

Tested whether the added member traces to a signed-off decision: string GetBaseDirectory() matches Decision 2 verbatim ('The member is string GetBaseDirectory(); on IEnvironment in AgentGuard.Abstractions') with Tim's cited yes; the interface's trailing-separator doc (IEnvironment.cs:47-53) matches Decision 5 ('the interface documents that guarantee'). Tested whether NotSupportedException (instead of the workflow's usual NotImplementedException) is a suppression or a rule-dodge: it is a non-flagged exception type, not a #pragma/[SuppressMessage]/NoWarn/severity edit; forced because MA0025 (Meziantou.Analyzer 3.0.125) flags NotImplementedException and Directory.Build.props sets TreatWarningsAsErrors=true + AnalysisMode=All; it matches the repo's own stub convention (PlatformNotSupportedException in PosixFileSystem.cs / WindowsFileSystem.cs) and is transparently documented in a code comment. The final code will not throw once IMPLEMENT fills it, so MA0025's target defect never ships. Not a suppression, not an evasion.

Checked whether the pre-existing S5443 [SuppressMessage] on GetTempDirectory was extended to cover the new member: git diff shows it is unchanged and scoped only to GetTempDirectory (EnvironmentAdapter.cs:39-43). Not extended.

Checked for any new type/member added beyond the contract: git diff of the three files shows ONLY the GetBaseDirectory member, its interface doc, and the Create baseDirectory param/doc.
